affectedPublicSurfaces: api.app-juli.com GET /v1/auth/tiktok/start — a NEW authenticated route. It did not exist before this change (verified: 404 in production), so there is no prior behaviour to regress, only a new door to get right.

api.app-juli.com GET /v1/auth/tiktok/callback — unchanged path, changed owner binding. A callback carrying a state now binds the shop to the user that state names and can no longer reach the shared app-review row; a state that is unsigned, wrongly signed, minted for another flow, or older than 10 minutes is refused with 401 where a signed-but-undated one used to be accepted.

demo.app-juli.com /v1/* — previously served by Next.js and 404ing; now proxied to the juli_api upstream. This makes GET /v1/shops (already called by the connect-shop screen) and GET /v1/auth/tiktok/start reachable from the demo origin for the first time.

demo.app-juli.com /connect (apps/demo ConnectShopView) — the 'Kết nối TikTok Shop' control changes from aria-disabled with an onClick that calls preventDefault into a live control that navigates the browser to TikTok Partner Center.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: the operator's own signed-in Google identity; no other seller is routed to the candidate

assertions: the response is 401, not a minted state

assertions: the authorize URL is https, on the TikTok partner host, and carries app_key, redirect_uri and state
verify_state on that state returns exactly the caller's user id
two different signed-in sellers get two states naming themselves

journeys.name: a-forged-or-stale-state-binds-nothing
journeys.entryUrl: unit: a state signed with a different secret, and a validly signed state past its TTL

journeys.name: demo-origin-reaches-v1

migrationCompatibility.notes: No migration and no schema change — deliberately, since issues #1964/#1965 hold migrations 064/065 and are changing `users`. The only writes are through the existing provision_shop_and_credentials path into existing `shops` and `tiktok_credentials` columns. A stable and a candidate release can run side by side: the candidate accepts only states it minted itself (same TIKTOK_APP_SECRET, so either instance can verify the other's), and the stable release has no state minter at all.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: redeploy the prior release. The route disappears and the demo connect button 404s — i.e. back to the pre-#1970 state, which is the current production behaviour. Shops already connected under the candidate keep their correct owner; nothing written by this change needs unwinding. The nginx vhost is deployed separately from the API and can be reverted on its own with `nginx -t && nginx -s reload`.

doNotInfer: Do not read the two-owner test as proof of tenant isolation. The `session` fixture is SQLite in-memory; it proves the owner column gets the right value, and nothing at all about Row Level Security, because SQLite has none. The Postgres-backed lanes (full-regression, Release-shape regression) are the only place RLS is exercised.

Do not treat the signed state as replay-proof. There is no server-side single-use nonce ledger — adding one needs storage this slice had no migration authority for. Replay inside the 10-minute TTL is bounded only by TikTok's single-use authorization code and by provision_shop_and_credentials refusing to rebind an already-owned shop.

Do not re-include /etc/nginx/juli/api-upstream.conf in the demo vhost to 'make it self-contained'. nginx upstreams are http-context and shared; a second include is a hard duplicate-upstream error that stops nginx loading ANY site (reproduced locally). A separately-named copy is worse: the API lane alternates 8000/8020 at each blue/green cutover, so the copy would go stale and point the demo at a dead port.

Do not conclude the stateless app-review path was fixed. #1748's carve-out is unchanged: outside production a callback with no state still binds to _app_review_user_id(). What changed is that the seller-initiated branch returns before reaching it, so a connect that HAS a state can never land there.

Do not deploy the nginx change as part of the API release. infra/nginx is not in release.yml; the owner applies vhost changes by hand, and both api.app-juli.com.conf and demo.app-juli.com.conf must be present in sites-enabled for the demo /v1 proxy to resolve its upstream.
